slides.headline: Neck sore by 3pm every day?
slides.sub: It's probably not your posture. Here's what actually helps.

slides.title: The real culprit: staying still
slides.body: Your neck can handle almost any position for a while. What it doesn't love is the same position for hours. Sitting 'perfectly' for eight hours still leaves you stiff.

slides.title: Move every 30 to 45 minutes
slides.body: Stand up, roll your shoulders, look over each shoulder, take a sip of water. Thirty seconds is enough. A timer beats good intentions.

slides.title: Raise the screen, not your chin
slides.body: If your screen sits below eye level, your head drifts forward and your neck muscles work overtime. A stack of books under the laptop is a fine start.

slides.title: Build the tolerance, not just the fix
slides.body: Simple strengthening for the neck and upper back twice a week makes a desk day feel shorter. Most people notice a difference within a few weeks.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Pain spreading down the arm, pins and needles, weakness in the hand, or headaches that keep building are worth an assessment rather than a guess.

slides.headline: Sick of the 3pm neck?
slides.body: Our physios assess how you sit, move and load your neck, then give you a short plan you'll actually stick to. Chatswood and Sydney CBD.

caption:
Neck sore by 3pm every day? It's probably not your posture. 🪑

Necks cope with most positions for a while. What they struggle with is the same position for hours on end. That's why the 'sit up straight' advice rarely fixes anything on its own.

What tends to help: moving every 30 to 45 minutes, getting your screen up to eye level, and a couple of short strengthening sessions a week so your neck can handle a full day. Pain spreading into the arm, pins and needles, or headaches that keep building are worth getting assessed.
